region: Platform: path/sandbox security, registry, deploy, CLI, git, databricks
purpose: The "platform/operations" layer of haute: everything between the pipeline-graph core and the outside world (filesystem, git, Databricks, Docker, MLflow, CLI). It enforces the security boundary for user-authored code and file access (AST sandbox + restricted unpickler + project-root path validation), holds the single-source-of-truth node dispatch registry (exec vs codegen), estimates RAM before training to avoid OOM, wraps all git CLI behind guardrails for non-technical users, caches Databricks tables to local parquet, and packages a pipeline as a live scoring API (Databricks Model Serving or a generated FastAPI container) with a test-before-live gate and a staging-vs-production impact report. The `haute` CLI (Click) is the operator surface over all of this.

invariants: Sandbox containment: validate_user_code MUST reject every known CPython sandbox-escape vector (dunder attribute access, __builtins__ subscript, getattr/type/vars/super, frame/traceback walks, import/class/async/global/nonlocal) BEFORE exec(); safe_globals MUST strip __import__/open/eval/exec/compile/etc. The two layers are defence-in-depth — neither alone is sufficient.

Path containment: validate_project_path and validate_safe_path MUST resolve() first and reject any path not is_relative_to(project_root); resolution must never escape the sandbox root via .., symlinks, or embedded NUL bytes.

resolve_runtime_file_path with enforce_project_root=True (HTTP routes) MUST raise/return-None for absolute or relative paths escaping the project root; existing files win over missing candidates and prefer breaks ties deterministically.

Restricted unpickler: safe_unpickle/safe_joblib_load MUST only construct globals whose (module,name) is in _ALLOWED_PICKLE_PREFIXES; single-segment prefixes match the package and dotted submodules but not lookalikes (numpy not numpy_evil).

Registry completeness: every NodeType MUST have BOTH an exec and a codegen builder (validate_registry_complete); duplicate registration MUST fail loudly; get_exec/get_codegen MUST raise (never silently fall back) on a missing entry so exec and codegen can never disagree.

Databricks cache safety: _cache_path_for MUST collapse a table name to one path component inside CACHE_DIR (reject traversal); fetch_and_cache MUST write to a unique temp file then atomically replace, and MUST raise FetchIntegrityError rather than cache when a retried batch lost rows (cursor.rownumber != rows_received) or a zero-row result carries no schema. SELECT clause MUST start with SELECT and contain no ;/--/ /* / dangerous keywords; table name MUST match catalog.schema.table.

Git guardrails: protected branches (main/master/develop/production, or HAUTE_PROTECTED_BRANCHES) MUST never be mutated; user-supplied refs/SHAs MUST pass _validate_ref_name (no leading '-', no control/glob/path chars) before reaching git CLI to prevent argument injection; destructive ops (revert/delete) MUST create + push a backup tag first; raw subprocess stderr MUST NOT reach HTTP (wrapped in GitError, sanitized) while authored messages use GitDomainError/GitGuardrailError.

Local session auth: real /api/* requests and websockets MUST present the per-process session token (hmac.compare_digest) and a trusted (loopback/configured) Origin, unless HAUTE_DISABLE_LOCAL_SESSION_AUTH is set; OPTIONS preflight is exempt.

Deploy test-before-live: deploy() MUST resolve -> validate_deploy (which scores every test quote and checks declared input schema + expected outputs) before dispatching; any structural or test-quote failure aborts with an aggregated DeployError. handle_deploy MUST block non-dry-run deploys outside CI.
Deploy reproducibility: container-based targets MUST use a patch- or digest-pinned base_image (validated at __post_init__ AND resolve_config); Dockerfile deps MUST be pinned to installed versions.

Deploy semantic preservation: the deployed scorer MUST reuse the dev execution engine and MUST verify the live input schema against the bundled feature contract at load time (assert_contracts_match); it MUST NOT manufacture predictions when a contract is bundled but the model artifact is absent (raises).

RAM guardrail conservatism: estimate_safe_training_rows returns no limit when source rows or column schema are unknown (None), and otherwise downsamples to >= _MIN_SAFE_ROWS so the estimate never silently trains on a dataset that won't fit; estimate is metadata-only (parquet footer), never executes the pipeline.

Bundler determinism: collect_artifacts MUST resolve every artifact path to an absolute path where the pipeline-relative file wins over CWD, and MUST raise (FileNotFoundError/DeployError) for missing artifacts or static-source schema drift rather than bundling a wrong file.

Impact correctness: percent-change math MUST refuse zero production baselines with non-zero staging (raises), MUST reject non-finite predictions, and MUST refuse truncated endpoint responses so the report never understates pricing impact.

candidate_risks.concern: Executor resolves pipeline-config file paths WITHOUT enforce_project_root, so a pipeline can read/scan files anywhere on the host filesystem at execution time
candidate_risks.why: execution.py:179 (canonical_dataframe_execution_graph) and execution.py:406 (_runtime_path_from_graph_config) call resolve_runtime_file_path(..., prefer='project') with enforce_project_root defaulting to False, unlike the HTTP routes which pass enforce_project_root=True. read_data_source/scan_parquet then open the resolved path. If pipeline graph JSON is ever attacker-influenced (e.g. an imported/shared pipeline, or a route that builds a graph from request data before the route-level path check), arbitrary-file read is possible. May be an intentional trust boundary (pipeline source is trusted code) but the asymmetry with the route layer is a sharp edge worth auditing.

candidate_risks.concern: _get_project_root() caches Path.cwd() at first call as a process-global; every path-containment check depends on it being correct
candidate_risks.why: _PROJECT_ROOT is lazily set to cwd at the time of the first _get_project_root() call (_sandbox.py:46-51). If any import-time or early code triggers resolution before the server has chdir'd to the real project, or if the server process cwd is broader than the intended root, validate_project_path/validate_safe_path silently authorize a wider tree. The value is mutable via set_project_root but there is no assertion that it matches the active pipeline's project; a stale or over-broad root weakens every downstream containment invariant.
candidate_risks.location: src/haute/_sandbox.py:43-72; routes use _get_project_root() at routes/_helpers.py:88 and routes/pipeline.py:383

candidate_risks.concern: safe_unpickle/safe_joblib_load still execute pickle reduce machinery for allowlisted modules; allowlist is broad (whole numpy/sklearn/scipy/pandas/joblib trees)
candidate_risks.why: RestrictedUnpickler only filters find_class by module prefix (_sandbox.py:380-413). Pickle remains code-bearing: numpy/sklearn contain reachable callables, and __reduce__ payloads of allowlisted classes can still drive object construction. The module docstring acknowledges payloads should be 'trusted', but load_external_object (_io.py:563) exposes this to any externalFile node path the pipeline references. A malicious .pkl placed in-project (or via a path that passes validate_project_path) is only weakly contained.

candidate_risks.concern: _validation_cache is an unbounded module-level dict keyed by the full code string
candidate_risks.why: _validate_user_code_cached (_sandbox.py:273,296-323) stores every distinct safe code string forever. In a long-lived server that previews/traces many distinct user code fragments (each edit is a new key), this grows without bound — a slow memory leak and a place where two threads race on the dict (guarded by a lock, but unbounded). Low security impact, but a correctness/resource lead.

candidate_risks.concern: Atomic cache replace uses Path.replace across a temp file in the same dir, but read_cached_table/scan_parquet readers are not coordinated with concurrent fetch replace on Windows
candidate_risks.why: fetch_and_cache writes tmp then tmp_path.replace(out_path) (_databricks_io.py:316,405). On Windows, os.replace fails if the destination is open by a reader (scan_parquet holds the file). Two concurrent fetches ('last finished wins') plus an active reader can raise PermissionError on replace, or a reader can observe the pre-replace file. The comment in _cache_path_for (lines 155-168) already documents Windows resolve() races; the replace-vs-open race is a related concurrency lead.

candidate_risks.concern: _assert_no_rows_lost_after_retry only arms AFTER the first retry; the very first fetchmany_arrow attempt has no row-accounting
candidate_risks.why: fetch_was_retried gates the integrity check (_databricks_io.py:339,361-368). The reasoning is that only a failed-then-retried batch can have advanced cursor.rownumber. But it relies on cursor.rownumber being an accurate DBAPI count and on the first successful batch being complete. If the connector ever advances rownumber on a partially-consumed first batch that did NOT raise (driver quirk), rows could be dropped silently because the check is skipped. Worth verifying the connector contract.

candidate_risks.concern: RAM/VRAM detection silently falls back to a fixed 4 GiB / None, and width estimation divides by row_count
candidate_risks.why: available_ram_bytes returns a hard 4 GiB on any failure (_ram_estimate.py:114-126) — on a small CI box or container with cgroup limits not reflected in /proc/meminfo MemAvailable, the estimate can be wildly off, causing either OOM (under-estimate of usage vs real cap) or needless downsampling. Variable-width column estimation does math.ceil(uncompressed_size / meta.row_count) guarded by row_count>0 (line 802-807), but mixed-source max() merging across nodes and the Float64 8-byte assumption for non-string columns can under-count wide string features. Numerical-correctness lead for the downsample decision.

candidate_risks.concern: _get_user_slug falls back to os.getlogin() and _is_own_branch/read-only logic depends on the slug matching exactly
candidate_risks.why: Read-only enforcement (get_status, _is_own_branch at _git.py:257-259,379) decides whether a branch is the user's by string-prefix pricing/<slug>/. _get_user_slug uses git config user.name then os.getlogin() (line 196-202). If git user.name differs between create_branch time and a later session (or os.getlogin differs in a service context), a user can be locked out of their own branch or, conversely, two users with colliding slugs share write access. Authorization-by-string-prefix is brittle; worth auditing against the route layer's guardrails.

candidate_risks.concern: _build_compare_url SSH→HTTPS rewrite and host detection are substring-based and could embed an attacker-controlled remote URL into a returned link
candidate_risks.why: _build_compare_url (_git.py:284-310) string-replaces git@ -> https:// and detects host by 'github'/'gitlab' substring in the URL. A crafted remote URL (e.g. https://evil-github.com.attacker.net/...) matches 'github' and is returned as a compare link surfaced to the user. Low severity (informational link, not an auth boundary) but a phishing/SSRF-adjacent lead.

candidate_risks.concern: Output-schema dry-run cache in .haute_cache/output_schema.json is keyed only by graph_fingerprint and silently ignored on read error
candidate_risks.why: infer_output_schema (deploy/_schema.py:95-150) caches the inferred output schema keyed by graph fingerprint. If the fingerprint does not capture an input that changes output dtypes (e.g. an external file's content, a data-source schema, or model artifact), a stale schema is reused and baked into the MLflow ModelSignature / manifest, producing a deployed contract that disagrees with reality. Cache write failure is swallowed (line 147-148, acceptable) but the read-side staleness is a silent-correctness lead.

candidate_risks.concern: validate_deploy runs test quotes through score_graph WITHOUT artifact_paths/remap, so MLflow-sourced model/optimiser nodes are exercised differently at validate-time than at serve-time
candidate_risks.why: score_test_quotes (deploy/_validators.py:375-380) and infer_output_schema (deploy/_schema.py:134) call score_graph with no artifact_paths. The scorer's modelScore/optimiserApply MLflow branches (deploy/_scorer.py:561-598,605-672) only engage with remap/MLflow source; with no remap a registered/run model node may load via its own config path or behave as a passthrough. The 'test before live' gate therefore may not exercise the exact bundled artifacts that the deployed container/pyfunc uses (which DO pass artifact_paths). Gap between validated and shipped behaviour.

candidate_risks.concern: Generated container app.py is produced by f-string templating of model_name/port into a large source blob
candidate_risks.why: _generate_app_source (deploy/_container.py:241-444) builds the FastAPI app via an f-string. model_name is validated by _VALID_MODEL_NAME_RE (^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$) before use (lines 43-46,94) and port is int — so injection is mitigated — but the pattern (codegen by string interpolation of config into executable Python) is fragile: any future field threaded into the template without equivalent validation becomes a container-build code-injection vector. Worth a focused review that every interpolated value is constrained.

candidate_risks.concern: collect_artifacts mutates the caller's node config dict in place (config['artifact_path'] = basename)
candidate_risks.why: In the MODEL_SCORE branch the bundler writes config["artifact_path"] = Path(artifact_path).name (deploy/_bundler.py:101) on the live pruned-graph node. Since pruned_graph is model_copy'd from full_graph and node.data.config is a shared dict, this in-place patch can leak the rewritten (basename-only) path back into objects that expect the original path, and makes collect_artifacts non-idempotent (a second call sees the already-shortened path and may build a different artifact key). Silent-state-mutation lead.

candidate_risks.concern: _live_only_edges label-matching for liveSwitch may pick the wrong live branch when input_scenario_map is absent
candidate_risks.why: prune_for_deploy keeps only the live branch of liveSwitch nodes by matching _sanitize_func_name(source label) against the configured live input name (deploy/_pruner.py:36-79). The fallback path (inputs[0] from config) matches by sanitized label, which can collide if two upstream nodes sanitize to the same name, silently selecting the wrong source for the deployed scoring path — a quiet semantic divergence between dev and deployed pricing. The non-fallback path raises on no match (good), but the fallback path does not.

candidate_risks.concern: _is_local_origin returns True when the Origin header is absent
candidate_risks.why: _is_local_origin (_local_security.py:142-147) treats a missing Origin as local/trusted, and LocalSessionMiddleware then still requires the token. So token is the real gate, but non-browser clients (curl, native apps, server-side request forgery via a tool that omits Origin) bypass the Origin check entirely and rely solely on the token. If the token ever leaks (it is also accepted as a URL query param, SESSION_TOKEN_QUERY_PARAM, which can land in logs/referrers), the Origin defence-in-depth is void. Token-in-query-string is the sharper lead.

candidate_risks.concern: _apply_env_overrides / from_cli_args bypass __post_init__ base-image pinning, relying on resolve_config to re-check
candidate_risks.why: DeployConfig.__post_init__ validates pinning, but override(), _apply_env_overrides, and direct attribute writes mutate target/base_image afterward (deploy/_config.py:425-465). The code correctly re-validates in resolve_config (lines 530-531), so the live deploy path is covered — but any caller that constructs a ResolvedDeploy or calls deploy_resolved/build_and_push_image without going through resolve_config (e.g. a future programmatic path or test helper) skips pinning. Defence depends on a single chokepoint that is easy to route around.

complexity_hotspots.what: Column-set resolution for the RAM estimate: recursive BFS through ancestors with edgeJoin column-derivation, coalesce/suffix handling, selected_columns filtering, per-column variable-width estimation, and the final peak-bytes/downsample decision. Deeply interlocking helpers (_resolve_target_columns_detail, _resolve_edge_join_columns, _edge_join_key_columns_on_path, _estimate_base_bytes_per_row, estimate_safe_training_rows).

score_graph_lazy: the deploy runtime engine. Builds NodeBuildHooks closures intercepting apiInput/externalFile/optimiserApply(file+MLflow)/modelScore(bundled+contract-only)/static dataSource, wires the dataframe execution cache, preamble compilation, contract verification, temp-path lifecycle, and execution-context admission. Many nested closures capturing per-node config with default-arg binding.

The public git API: status/branch/save/history/revert/pull/submit/archive/delete, each orchestrating multiple _run_git/_run_git_ok calls with fetch throttling+serialization locks, backup-tag-before-destructive ordering, remote-branch existence probing, and conflict abort/rollback in pull_latest. State machine over the working tree with concurrency locks.

The AST validator and its blocked-name frozensets (_BLOCKED_ATTRS/_BLOCKED_FRAME_ATTRS/_BLOCKED_CALLS) plus the cached validate path with code-wrapping fallback. Security-critical and adversarial — the completeness of the blocklists is the whole containment story.

fetch_and_cache: Arrow-batch streaming with exponential-backoff retry, mid-fetch row-loss integrity assertion, zero-row schema-terminator handling, temp-file-then-atomic-replace, thread-safe progress tracking, and BaseException cleanup. Concurrency + integrity logic concentrated here.

TOML schema validation (recursive _check with _self/sub-section model), DeployConfig.from_toml field assembly across 7 sub-configs + env overrides, and resolve_config orchestration (parse -> find output -> prune -> find inputs -> collect artifacts -> infer schemas).

Hand-rolled TOML scanners (_scan_table_headers, _find_project_table_bounds, _find_matching_bracket, _rewrite_project_dependencies) that string-walk pyproject.toml tracking string/comment state to inject the haute dependency without a TOML writer. Parser-style state machine.

Host-binding safety (loopback detection across IPv4/IPv6/hostname), trusted-host derivation, port pre-flight with SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE on Windows, TCP readiness probing, Vite subprocess lifecycle with signal handlers, and dev-vs-prod mode selection.

internal_dataflow: IN: (1) CLI invocation -> _project.resolve_pipeline_file maps a user path/None to a concrete .py -> parser.parse_pipeline_file -> PipelineGraph. (2) HTTP requests -> _local_security middleware (token + Origin gate) -> routes -> _git operations / file reads via validate_safe_path. (3) Deploy: haute.toml + .env + CLI flags -> DeployConfig (from_toml/from_cli_args + env overrides) -> resolve_config -> parse pipeline -> prune_for_deploy (live-branch-only ancestors of the output node) -> find_deploy_input_nodes -> collect_artifacts (download MLflow models, bundle feature contracts, verify static-source schema) -> infer_input_schema (read source footer) + infer_output_schema (1-row dry-run through score_graph, fingerprint-cached) -> ResolvedDeploy. (4) Databricks: node http_path + env creds -> fetch_and_cache streams Arrow batches to local .haute_cache/<table>.parquet; runtime reads via read_cached_table -> scan_parquet. (5) Training: PipelineGraph + target node -> estimate_safe_training_rows reads ancestor parquet footers only. OUT: validate_deploy aggregates structural + test-quote errors into DeployError (gate); on pass, deploy_resolved -> _dispatch_resolved -> deploy_to_mlflow (build_manifest -> mlflow.pyfunc.log_model with _model_code.py + conda env + signature -> register UC model -> create/update serving endpoint) OR deploy_to_container (build_manifest -> generate app.py + Dockerfile -> docker build/push). At serve time the generated app / pyfunc call deploy._scorer.score_graph, which reuses haute.execution.execute_lazy_graph with NodeBuildHooks that inject the live input DataFrame, remap artifact paths, and assert the live schema matches the bundled feature contract. impact command scores a safety dataset through staging+prod endpoints and emits build_report -> format_terminal/markdown (-> GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY). The node registry (_registry) is populated as an import side-effect of _builders + _codegen_builders and validated complete before any exec/codegen dispatch.
concurrency_model: Predominantly synchronous, single-process. Explicit locks: _sandbox._validation_cache_lock (guards the unbounded validation cache), _sandbox._joblib_lock (serializes the monkeypatch of joblib NumpyUnpickler.find_class — a process-global mutation window, risky if other joblib loads run concurrently), _git._fetch_time_lock + _fetch_exec_lock (throttle and serialize `git fetch` so two callers don't race the local object store), _databricks_io._fetch_lock (guards _fetch_progress dict). Deploy scorer relies on StatGatedCache per-key locking so a thundering herd of /quote requests on container start performs exactly one disk load per artifact; cached values are treated as immutable and shared across request threads. The generated FastAPI container serves /quote concurrently (async endpoint reads body, then synchronous polars execution under an admitted ExecutionContext); NDJSON streaming path yields batches via bounded_collect_batches. fetch_and_cache uses unique mkstemp temp files + atomic Path.replace so concurrent fetches of the same table don't interleave ('last finished wins'). _get_project_root / _PROJECT_ROOT is a process-global with no lock (set once, then read) — fine if set before threads start, a hazard if mutated mid-flight. _get_default_branch_cached uses lru_cache keyed on stringified cwd.
perf_characteristics: RAM estimate is intentionally cheap: reads only parquet footers (read_parquet_metadata), never materializes data — replaced an older 1000-row probe approach. Git status throttles `git fetch` to once per 30s (_FETCH_COOLDOWN_SECONDS) and uses %(ahead-behind:ref) to get branch counts in one subprocess (git>=2.35) with a per-branch fallback; default-branch detection is lru_cached per cwd. Databricks fetch streams in 100k-row Arrow batches with zstd compression so memory stays bounded regardless of table size; subsequent reads get full scan_parquet predicate pushdown from the local cache. Deploy scorer stat-gates model + feature-contract loads (one disk load per artifact across all requests) and uses the dataframe execution cache for DEPLOY_BATCH (not DEPLOY_LIVE single-row). Output-schema inference is fingerprint-cached to .haute_cache/output_schema.json to skip the dry-run on unchanged pipelines. Impact scoring batches endpoint calls (default 500 rows/request). Costs concentrate in: MLflow model download at deploy time (cached under .cache/models/), docker build/push, and the per-request polars pipeline execution at serve time.
test_coverage_observations: Security boundary is heavily tested: tests/test_sandbox.py (~1700 lines), tests/test_path_traversal_advanced.py + test_path_traversal_fixes.py (symlink escape, NUL bytes, unicode dots, long paths, parametrized across validate_safe_path/validate_project_path/resolve_runtime_file_path), tests/test_path_resolution.py + test_path_resolution_properties.py + test_property.py (Hypothesis property tests asserting resolution never escapes root and slash/backslash equivalence). Many tests call set_project_root(tmp_path) directly and conftest.py provides fixtures (widening root to '/' for /tmp). RAM estimate, git, databricks, deploy each have dedicated suites (referenced by the source comments citing specific tests, e.g. test_deploy_config_and_bundle for path-precedence, W4b.9 for feature-contract naming). The deploy scorer's contract-mismatch and missing-artifact branches raise loudly (testable). Gaps to probe in a deeper audit: (1) the executor-path file resolution without enforce_project_root (asymmetry vs routes) — unclear if a test pins that pipeline execution stays in-root; (2) validate-vs-serve artifact_paths divergence in score_test_quotes; (3) Windows atomic-replace-vs-open race in the databricks cache; (4) liveSwitch fallback label-collision in the pruner; (5) stale output_schema cache when fingerprint misses an input. CLI commands are split into handle_* pure functions specifically to be unit-testable without Click.
